title: SMILE Pro & Visumax 800: The Future of Lenticule Extraction
summary: SMILE® Pro represents the latest evolution in refractive surgery, utilizing the ultra-fast 2MHz Visumax 800 femtosecond laser. This next-generation platform enhances surgical efficiency with AI-driven centration (CentraLign) and cyclotorsion compensation (OcuLign), reducing laser time to under 10 seconds per eye.

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Overview
sections.content: SMILE (Small Incision Lenticule Extraction) is a flapless, minimally invasive keratorefractive procedure. The Visumax 800 platform (SMILE Pro) utilizes a femtosecond laser to create a refractive lenticule within the intact corneal stroma, which is manually extracted through a peripheral 2-3mm incision. This preserves the anterior corneal biomechanical strength and reduces post-operative dry eye compared to LASIK.

branches: Preservation of Anterior 40% of Stroma (Strongest fibers)

sections.title: Clinical Indications
content: Myopia: -0.50 D to -10.00 D
Astigmatism: up to -5.00 D
Cylinder + Sphere: Total up to -12.50 D (Region dependent)
Stable refraction for at least 12 months
Patients with active lifestyles or contact sports
Patients with mild-to-moderate dry eye

sections.title: Absolute Contraindications
content: Keratoconus or Forme Fruste Keratoconus (FFKC)
Abnormal topography (e.g., Pellucid Marginal Degeneration)
Corneal thickness resulting in Residual Stromal Bed < 250 microns
Active ocular infection or severe inflammation
Uncontrolled systemic autoimmune disease
Pregnancy or nursing (due to refractive instability)

sections.title: The 'Pro' Workflow: Step-by-Step
content: 1. Docking: Curved contact glass interfaces with the cornea to stabilize the globe.
2. CentraLign: The system automatically identifies the corneal vertex for precise centration.
3. OcuLign: The laser pattern rotates to compensate for cyclotorsion based on pre-op marks.
4. Posterior Surface: The laser creates the posterior border of the refractive lenticule.
5. Lenticule Side-Cut: Defines the edge of the lenticule.
6. Anterior Surface (Cap): The laser creates the upper boundary (usually at 120μm depth).
7. Entry Incision: A small 2.0-3.0mm incision is made at the 12 o'clock position (standard).
8. Dissection: The surgeon uses a 'SMILE separator' to free the lenticule.
9. Extraction: The lenticule is removed using micro-forceps.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Essentials
content: Pentacam/Galilei: Rule out ectasia via Belin-Ambrósio Enhanced Ectasia display.
Manifest vs Cycloplegic Refraction: Essential for accurate sphere/cylinder power.
Corneal Hysteresis (ORA): Optional, assesses biomechanical health.
Epithelial Mapping: Thickening over thin areas can mask underlying ectasia.
Meibography/TBUT: Baseline dry eye status assessment.

branches: Suction Loss (Significantly reduced with VM800 speed)
Cap Tear (Usually at entry incision site)

rows: Observation or irrigation of the interface
Circle software (convert to LASIK) or Surface Ablation (PRK)

content.explanation: P: Posterior plane dissection first. A: Anterior plane dissection second. S: Sweep across the lenticule. E: Extract the lenticule.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Lenticule Thickness: Aim for >15μm for easier extraction (avoids tearing).
Cap Thickness: Standard is 120μm; thicker caps are easier for beginners.
CentraLign Benefit: Reduces induced coma and higher-order aberrations.
Bubble Management: If OBL is present, wait 10 seconds before starting dissection.

Nests of cells crawling from edge

sections.title: Recent Advances: The Visumax 800 Advantage
sections.content: The introduction of the Visumax 800 has addressed the 'stress factor' of SMILE. By reducing laser time from 28 seconds to roughly 8-9 seconds, the risk of patient-induced suction loss is dramatically decreased. Furthermore, the integration of preoperative topography data with the laser’s heads-up display allows for 'digital marking' of the eye, making the correction of astigmatism far more reliable than manual marking techniques used with older models.
